newsitem.title: USA: Union says Tosco contract may not pass.
newsitem.headline: Union says Tosco contract may not pass.

text.p: Leaders of the Oil, Chemical, and Atomic Workers International Union (OCAW) on Wednesday said a tentative labor contract with Tosco Corp may not be approved by union members.
Although union negotiators agreed earlier this week to a new contract, local officials said concerns about the number of layoffs could jeopardize the pact.
"It's going to be a very close vote," said Kelly Quinn, president of the union's Los Angeles branch, which expects to vote against the contract.

The union had threatened to strike last week but the threat was withdrawn after a meeting with Tosco officials on Monday. The company reportedly told union officials it would lay off as many as 370 employees and shut down a refinery in Rodeo, Calif. unless the union agreed to participate in an overall cost reduction program.
On Monday, Tosco will acquire Unocal Corp's four California refineries. Although Unocal still owns the plants, the company asked Unocal managers to lay off as many as 140 employees.
Since Tuesday, Unocal has put about 90 workers on paid administrative leave, a precursor to firing, union officials said.
Union members will vote on the contract Thursday and Friday. ((David Brinkerhoff, Los Angeles bureau +1 213 380 2014))
